propositions: Three separate code paths (normal compaction, rebuild, crash recovery) each re-derive identical candidate listing, snapshot detection, envelope building, retired-file restoration, and commit logic, creating maintenance burden and divergence risk.

Snapshot envelope construction and source-uuid filtering logic appear duplicated across compact_txn, compact_rebuild, and inline in compact_txn, with bug fixes (aea0 source-uuid exclusion) unevenly applied.
Retired file restoration and rename-back logic in compact_txn, compact_recovery, and rollback paths independently implement the same data-loss guard (e72e) and commit semantics.
A shared compact_plan module consolidates candidate discovery, snapshot detection, envelope building, and retire/commit operations as callable functions routed through all three compaction paths.
The rebuild's idempotent .snapshot-rebuild.bak crash model and per-file tolerance are intentionally preserved; only shared derivation logic moves to the planner, not abort-and-rollback semantics.

Recorded convergence: list_candidates enforces .json suffix requirement that rebuild already checked, filtering stray non-event files that were previously cited in source_event_uuids and incorrectly retired.
